title: The best kind of theatre problem: seeing a new musical across the cou...
transcript: I'm on a West Coast theater trip that I designed specifically around seeing the lunchbox at Berkeley Rep, and let me tell you, it was definitely worth the trip. Music by the Lazars, directed by Rachel Chavkin. A romance between two unlikely people. Literally all my favorite thing. In fact, I ended up seeing it twice, once in previews and then a few days later on opening night. And I'm just so glad cause they actually did make a few changes and that is what I love the most about a world premiere. The musical is about a mistaken lunch box delivery in Moon Pie that connects a lonely widower and a mother trapped in an unhappy marriage. They begin sharing moments of their lives through notes tucked inside these lunch boxes and find a deep connection when they both need it most. The Lunch Box is all heart and emotion, but is also extremely funny and filled with quirky characters. Actually reminded me a lot of waitress. Music is gorgeous. The Lazarus have written some of my favorite new scores in recent years. This is no exception and actually might be my favorite one yet. I have been humming it non stop and I need a cast recording immediately. The set is so cool, it literally feels like you are in the streets of Mumbai. And I just love the choreography and the costumes and of course the performances are everything. Koo Koo Burma is very much the heart. Of this show, the frustration she feels, her longing, her resilience. She makes so many small, specific choices and is so captivating. And, of course, Rachel Chapman directing. All the things I love most about her work are displayed in this. The innovative staging and storytelling, the ability to make something feel both grand and in the perfect mix of complex feelings and humor. The lunchbox has it all. And if you are going to be in the Bay Area over the next few weeks, you. You cannot miss it. There is truly nothing like seeing a musical make its world premiere, watching it find itself and take shape, and getting to play a small role just by being in that audience. I'm so happy I made the trip to Berkeley Rep. And I hope this is only the beginning of a beautiful journey for this new musical. Go see the lunchbox.
